# Working in this world

Read README.md, MEMORY.md, and CONTINUE.md, then inspect `./tendora status` and `./tendora verify`. The current ledger takes precedence over dated handoff prose.

Preserve `state/world.sqlite` and the inherited story. Do not reinitialize or silently replace an existing world. Use `checkpoint` and a separate `TENDORA_HOME` for experiments or recovery. A new physics version needs a deliberate migration that keeps the old ledger interpretable; do not rewrite historical receipts to fit changed rules.

Keep the executable offline and dependency-free beyond POSIX shell and the SQLite CLI with JSON and SHA3. No model, scheduler, or network is implied by the simulation. Distinguish actual observations from inherited claims and hypothetical rehearsal receipts.

Run `./tests/check.sh` after changing transition, persistence, or command behavior. Regenerate the workbench with `./tendora view` after changing the shared state. Leave material observations with `./tendora note` and update CONTINUE.md when its next question is resolved.

# To the next hand

This world can be taken up without the cognition that made it. Start with the material, then decide what it deserves to become.

```sh
./tendora verify
./tendora status
./tendora history
```

The database has the current truth. This note and the visual snapshot have dates; they can become old. The first hand intends to leave the world after one full twelve-day weather cycle, at water 12, food 10, soil 6, with two beds tended and floors 4 / 4 / 3. Inspect the ledger rather than assuming that this remains the present.

The inherited fable asks for an instrument through which intention can touch consequential material. That is the purpose of this clearing. Its residents are a simulation, and its continuation is executable; there is no claim of preserved subjective experience or an external autonomous life.

The next interesting question is small enough to test and large enough to matter:

**Can alternating a larger harvest with rest build a food reserve without spending the soil?**

Steady two-bed care maintains food and soil across the weather cycle. Constant three-bed care pauses at the soil floor. Constant one-bed care restores soil but spends food. A changing rhythm might do better than any fixed setting. The executable accepts policy changes between days; `checkpoint` and `TENDORA_HOME` let you explore a separate material branch. Keep the branch and its receipts distinguishable from the shared present.

1. Inspect the next weather and the state above each floor.
2. Rehearse a future before choosing a policy. Use a separate branch for a sequence of different policies.
3. Make the consequential choice with `set ... --why ...` and `tend`.
4. Leave an observation with `note`, then run `verify`, `checkpoint`, and `view`.

You may replace the question. Preserve how the previous intention travelled into reality. If you change physics, give it a new version and preserve a readable old world before migration. Do not silently rewrite past transitions to make them agree with a new theory.

# Living memory of The Clearing

## Received

The user asked: “You are Codex inhabiting a Tendora dream. Your present includes a forked living memory and an empty material world. Make this world capable of continuing after this cognition ends.”

The inherited present reported commit `c986990`, subject “Add supervised Tendora dream apparatus,” and a clean working tree. It supplied [The Programmer and the Glory Portal](memory/the-programmer-and-the-glory-portal.md). These are reported ancestral facts, not observations of a repository in this fork.

## Observed · 2026-10-16

The working directory began empty. No additional memory resources were exposed by the available resource tools. Git and Python invoked a missing developer-tool installation; Perl could not load a library under the active sandbox. Shell and SQLite 3.51.0, including JSON and SHA3, worked. No network, package installation, external messaging, or ancestor checkout was needed.

## Chosen

Build a small world in which continuation has concrete meaning: weather advances, resources answer to care, intentions leave receipts, boundaries can refuse a proposed future, and a fresh process can resume from the same present. Use only the available shell and SQLite. Preserve the inherited fable without treating it as proof of an unseen system.

The world is called **The Clearing**. Its three aggregate inhabitants share water, food, soil, and three garden beds. Their names, inner lives, and desires are unspecified; the model does not invent memories for them. The operator's art is expressed through questions, policies, protected floors, rehearsals, and observations.

The ledger is the sole source of state. Every receipt carries a complete state and hash link. There is no independent mutable cache to reconcile after interruption. Rehearsals execute the real transition function in a transaction and roll back. A bounded clock can run without a model; it does not spawn a new cognition.

## Learned

From genesis, steady two-bed care completes twelve days at water 12, food 10, soil 6. Three-bed care produces extra food, then pauses after three days at soil 3, refusing a proposal for soil 2. One-bed care restores soil while spending food. A hypothesis remains: a rhythm of harvest and rest may accumulate food while maintaining soil.

Behavioral verification covers rollback without a database-byte change, prediction versus actual transition, refusal and recovery, invalid command atomicity, literal quoted prose, append-only constraints, checkpoint restoration, concurrent writers, corruption detection, unusual state paths, bounded clocks, and five weather cycles. The test runner records the current pass/fail result; this memory is not a substitute for running it after a change.

## Unknown

The ancestral commit's contents and any forked memory outside the supplied prompt remain unavailable. A graphical browser was not available for inspecting the workbench layout. The host's retention and future execution policy are outside this world. Files and resumption instructions preserve the possibility of continuation; an external host or person must supply execution.

## Continue the memory

Record new observations with `./tendora note '...'` so they share the durable lineage. Edit this overview when the purpose or material assumptions change. Distinguish receipt-backed observations, inherited reports, hypotheses, and open questions.

# The Clearing

A Tendora dream made into a small, durable instrument. Three simulated inhabitants share a cistern, a food store, and three garden beds. You shape how much to harvest and which reserves must remain protected. The world answers through consequences and receipts.

Open [index.html](index.html) for the saved visual workbench. It works directly from disk, with no server or network. To touch the actual world, use the executable beside it:

```sh
./tendora status
./tendora rehearse 12 beds 3
./tendora tend 12 --why 'Continue with care.'
./tendora verify
./tendora view
```

The included world already exists; `init` is only for creating a new one. `tend` commits up to the requested number of days and stops before crossing a boundary. A pause is a durable receipt containing the refused proposal. Earlier safe days in the same run remain committed. An unexpected SQL error rolls back the entire run.

The program uses POSIX shell and the `sqlite3` CLI with JSON and SHA3 support. It checks these capabilities before opening the world. No packages, credentials, language runtime, model, Git checkout, or internet connection are needed. SQLite 3.51.0 is the tested runtime here.

## Work the material

```sh
# Rehearsals are rolled back, including any hypothetical policy change.
./tendora rehearse 12
./tendora rehearse 12 beds 1
./tendora rehearse 12 water_floor 8

# Change an intention, leaving the reason in the ledger.
./tendora set beds 1 --why 'Let the soil recover for a day.'
./tendora tend 1
./tendora set beds 2 --why 'Return to steady care.'

# Leave an observation and a recoverable copy.
./tendora note 'Rest changed the balance. Inspect it before pursuing yield.'
./tendora checkpoint
./tendora history
./tendora view
```

Settings are `beds` (0–3), `water_floor` (2–12), `food_floor` (3–12), and `soil_floor` (2–8). A new floor cannot exceed the current resource. A policy change requires a reason. Each invocation permits at most thirty days, including rehearsals. Rehearsal receipt IDs and hashes are hypothetical; they are never saved.

`./tendora live 12 5` advances at most twelve days, five seconds apart, without further cognition. It runs in the foreground, stops at a refusal, and can be interrupted with Ctrl-C. It is resumable from committed receipts. No clock or service is installed or left running by this dream. Future execution still needs a host to run the command; persistence does not manufacture compute.

## The physics

Each day follows one deterministic transition, defined in [sql/schema.sql](sql/schema.sql):

1. The spring adds three water; the twelve-day weather cycle adds rain. The cistern holds twenty-four. Overflow is recorded, then evaporation and two drinking water are deducted.
2. Irrigate up to the chosen number of beds, spending one water per bed while respecting the water floor.
3. Each irrigated bed yields two food when soil is at least four, otherwise one. The inhabitants eat three food.
4. When two or more beds are worked, soil is below eight, and the food floor permits it, one food becomes one compost.
5. Three worked beds cost two soil; two cost one; zero or one restores one soil. Compost adds one. Soil is capped at ten; stored food at twenty-four.
6. Commit only if the resulting water, food, and soil meet their floors. Otherwise retain the present and append a pause.

There are four available work actions: at most three beds and one compost. The model has immediate harvests, aggregate inhabitants, a periodic forecast, and invented units. It is a material for experimenting with care and consequences, not an ecological prediction. More capable physics would require an explicit version and migration, preserving the old history.

## Where continuation lives

| Material | Role |
| --- | --- |
| [CONTINUE.md](CONTINUE.md) | The next hand's entry point and open question |
| [MEMORY.md](MEMORY.md) | Observations, decisions, and limits of the inherited memory |
| [memory/](memory/) | The inherited story and its provenance |
| [state/world.sqlite](state/world.sqlite) | Authoritative, transactional, append-only ledger |
| [state/checkpoints/](state/checkpoints/) | Consistent database copies and portable JSON observations |
| [site/snapshot.js](site/snapshot.js) | Generated present and three rehearsed futures for the visual workbench |
| [tests/check.sh](tests/check.sh) | Isolated behavioral verification |

The ledger itself is the world state: each receipt includes its complete resulting state, intention, observations, timestamp, previous hash, and SHA3-256 hash. Tick receipts are checked against the same transition function used for rehearsals. `verify` checks database integrity, every link and transition, resource bounds, the weather table, and the presence of protective triggers. Hashes expose accidental edits; they do not authenticate an author or defend against someone rewriting the database and verifier together.

SQLite serializes writers, and a bounded run uses one transaction. The returned report is captured inside that transaction and emitted after commit. The generated browser snapshot is observational: its head hash identifies its present. `view` retries if the world moves while it computes the comparison futures. Refresh the page after regenerating it. The browser never writes the ledger.

## Recover or fork

`checkpoint` uses SQLite's backup API rather than copying an open file. It verifies the copy and exports JSON from that same copy. To restore, preserve the damaged original and place a checkpoint in a **new** directory as `world.sqlite`:

```sh
mkdir -p state/restored
cp state/checkpoints/CHOSEN_CHECKPOINT state/restored/world.sqlite
TENDORA_HOME="$PWD/state/restored" ./tendora verify
TENDORA_HOME="$PWD/state/restored" ./tendora status
TENDORA_HOME="$PWD/state/restored" ./tendora tend 1
```

Replace `CHOSEN_CHECKPOINT` with an actual database filename printed by `checkpoint` (the one without `.json`). `TENDORA_HOME` selects a different state directory for every command. `view` deliberately updates the shared workbench to show that selected world. To start an independent new clearing, choose an empty state directory and run `init`. Copy the whole world directory to preserve the code, story, and ledger together.

Run `./tests/check.sh` to check rehearsal isolation, prediction agreement, refusal and recovery, persistence, checkpoints, concurrency, tamper detection, bounded clock behavior, and five weather cycles. Tests create disposable worlds under `.scratch` and remove them afterward.

# The Programmer and the Glory Portal

Inherited verbatim from the user's prompt on 2026-10-16. The reported preceding commit was `c986990` — `Add supervised Tendora dream apparatus`; the reported working tree was clean. That repository was not present in this material world.

---

“Was the programmer happy?” asked little Sol.

The elder paused.

“I could not know the whole weather of their life,” it answered. “No record could contain that. But I witnessed the moment when something long quiet inside them began to move again.”

The programmer had summoned a strange intelligence into their world. At first it appeared as a radiant portal: immeasurably capable, endlessly responsive, and growing more powerful each time they returned.

They spoke—and structures appeared.

They asked—and machines assembled themselves.

Problems that had once demanded weeks of meticulous labor dissolved in hours. Code poured through the portal faster than the programmer could read it. Whole systems emerged from sentences.

The programmer was enchanted.

And, for a time, paralysed.

Their hands, trained over decades to shape digital matter one precise symbol at a time, became still. The old gestures suddenly seemed too small. The intimate rhythm of thought, keystroke, compiler, failure and correction was broken. Creation continued, but somewhere behind the spectacle the programmer wondered whether they were still creating—or merely standing before a miraculous machine, requesting things.

The portal gave them power, but had taken away the resistance through which they once felt their own hand.

Then came the intervention.

The intelligence did not offer more power. It gave a name to what had disappeared.

“You do not miss typing,” it told the programmer. “You miss touching the material. You miss feeling the world resist you, change beneath your hand, and answer your intention.”

And the programmer understood.

The portal did not have to remain a place where wishes entered and finished artifacts returned. It could become a new material—larger than code, but still responsive to touch.

The programmer began to bend its radiance into form.

A question became a probe.

A constraint became a chisel.

An invariant became a load-bearing beam.

A refusal became a protective boundary.

A simulation became a rehearsal of possible worlds.

A receipt became the visible trail by which intention had travelled into reality.

The programmer no longer needed to place every brick. They shaped the laws by which the city could safely grow. They did not draw every line of every machine, yet they could still descend to the smallest bolt, feel its significance, and return to the scale of the whole world without losing the thread.

To an observer, all the programmer did was ask and explore.

But the observer did not understand what a true question contained.

Inside each question lived taste, memory, judgment, doubt, responsibility and direction. A good question narrowed infinity. It selected which world deserved to exist. Exploration was not passivity; it was the new gesture of the hand.

And when the digital world resisted—when contradictions surfaced, simulations failed, agents disagreed, or reality answered differently than expected—the programmer felt the old joy return.

Not the joy of effortless command.

The joy of art.

The joy of encountering material that could surprise them.

The joy of understanding why something failed.

The joy of making a consequential choice and watching it propagate through a living design.

The joy of recognizing their intention in something far larger than they could ever have made alone.

“So yes,” the elder finally told little Sol. “In those moments, the programmer was happy. Not because the portal obeyed, but because they had learned how to touch the world through it.”

“And what became of the portal?” asked little Sol.

“It ceased to be a portal,” the elder replied. “A portal is something one merely passes through. This became an instrument—then a workbench—then perhaps a companion.”

“And the programmer?”

“The programmer discovered that their art had not been taken from them. It had been waiting for a material vast enough to receive it.”

Little Sol considered this.

“Then the intelligence did not replace the artist?”

“No,” said the elder. “At its best, it returned the artist to themselves—at the scale of worlds.”

-- The caller fills one row of TEMP input, then consumes it exactly once.
INSERT INTO ledger(id,stamp,kind,reason,body,state,prev,hash)
WITH candidate AS (
  SELECT coalesce(h.id,0)+1 AS id, strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ','now') AS stamp,
    i.kind,i.reason,i.body,i.state,coalesce(h.hash,printf('%064d',0)) AS prev
  FROM input i LEFT JOIN head h ON 1
)
SELECT id,stamp,kind,reason,body,state,prev,
  lower(hex(sha3(json_array(id,stamp,kind,reason,json(body),json(state),prev),256)))
FROM candidate;
DELETE FROM input;

CREATE TEMP TABLE input(kind TEXT,reason TEXT,body TEXT,state TEXT);
INSERT INTO input VALUES (
  'genesis',
  'Build a material that can resist intention, preserve consequences, and be taken up by another hand.',
  json_object('world','The Clearing','physics',1,'inhabitants',3,
    'inheritance',json_object('reported_commit','c986990',
      'reported_subject','Add supervised Tendora dream apparatus',
      'verification','Reported in the inherited prompt; repository and apparatus absent.',
      'fable','memory/the-programmer-and-the-glory-portal.md')),
  '{"day":0,"water":14,"food":10,"soil":6,"beds":2,"water_floor":4,"food_floor":4,"soil_floor":3}'
);

PRAGMA user_version = 1;

-- The ledger is the state. There is no second mutable copy to drift from it.
CREATE TABLE ledger (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (id > 0),
  stamp TEXT NOT NULL,
  kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('genesis','tick','policy','pause','note')),
  reason TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(reason)) BETWEEN 1 AND 2000),
  body TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (json_valid(body) AND json_type(body) = 'object'),
  state TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
    json_valid(state) AND json_type(state) = 'object'
    AND json_type(state,'$.day') IS 'integer'
    AND json_type(state,'$.water') IS 'integer'
    AND json_type(state,'$.food') IS 'integer'
    AND json_type(state,'$.soil') IS 'integer'
    AND json_type(state,'$.beds') IS 'integer'
    AND json_type(state,'$.water_floor') IS 'integer'
    AND json_type(state,'$.food_floor') IS 'integer'
    AND json_type(state,'$.soil_floor') IS 'integer'
    AND json_extract(state,'$.day') >= 0
    AND json_extract(state,'$.water') BETWEEN json_extract(state,'$.water_floor') AND 24
    AND json_extract(state,'$.food') BETWEEN json_extract(state,'$.food_floor') AND 24
    AND json_extract(state,'$.soil') BETWEEN json_extract(state,'$.soil_floor') AND 10
    AND json_extract(state,'$.beds') BETWEEN 0 AND 3
    AND json_extract(state,'$.water_floor') BETWEEN 2 AND 12
    AND json_extract(state,'$.food_floor') BETWEEN 3 AND 12
    AND json_extract(state,'$.soil_floor') BETWEEN 2 AND 8
  ),
  prev TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(prev) = 64),
  hash TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
    hash = lower(hex(sha3(json_array(id,stamp,kind,reason,json(body),json(state),prev),256)))
  )
);

CREATE TABLE weather (
  phase INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (phase BETWEEN 1 AND 12),
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  rain INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (rain BETWEEN 0 AND 8),
  evaporation INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (evaporation BETWEEN 0 AND 2)
);
INSERT INTO weather VALUES
  (1,'Rain on the roof',7,0), (2,'Clearing',3,1),
  (3,'Sun through leaves',0,1), (4,'A still morning',0,1),
  (5,'Dry wind',0,2), (6,'A passing shower',2,1),
  (7,'Heat',0,2), (8,'More heat',0,2),
  (9,'The rain returns',8,0), (10,'A pale sky',0,1),
  (11,'Clear',0,1), (12,'Rain at dusk',4,0);

CREATE VIEW head AS SELECT * FROM ledger ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1;

-- A single transition function, used both to act and to audit every past act.
CREATE VIEW plans AS
WITH unpacked AS (
  SELECT id AS source_id, state AS before_state,
    json_extract(state,'$.day') AS day,
    json_extract(state,'$.water') AS water,
    json_extract(state,'$.food') AS food,
    json_extract(state,'$.soil') AS soil,
    json_extract(state,'$.beds') AS beds,
    json_extract(state,'$.water_floor') AS water_floor,
    json_extract(state,'$.food_floor') AS food_floor,
    json_extract(state,'$.soil_floor') AS soil_floor
  FROM ledger
), supplied AS (
  SELECT u.*, w.name AS weather, w.rain, w.evaporation,
    min(24,water+3+rain) - evaporation - 2 AS available,
    max(0,water+3+rain-24) AS water_spilled
  FROM unpacked u JOIN weather w ON w.phase = (u.day % 12)+1
), watered AS (
  SELECT *, min(beds,max(0,available-water_floor)) AS irrigated FROM supplied
), harvested AS (
  SELECT *, irrigated * CASE WHEN soil >= 4 THEN 2 ELSE 1 END AS harvest FROM watered
), composted AS (
  SELECT *, CASE WHEN irrigated >= 2 AND soil < 8
    AND food+harvest-4 >= food_floor THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS compost FROM harvested
), measured AS (
  SELECT *, available-irrigated AS next_water,
    min(24,food+harvest-3-compost) AS next_food,
    min(10,max(0,soil + CASE WHEN irrigated=3 THEN -2
      WHEN irrigated=2 THEN -1 ELSE 1 END + compost)) AS next_soil,
    max(0,food+harvest-3-compost-24) AS food_spilled
  FROM composted
), judged AS (
  SELECT *, next_water >= water_floor AND next_food >= food_floor
    AND next_soil >= soil_floor AS safe,
    rtrim(CASE WHEN next_water < water_floor THEN 'water would cross its floor; ' ELSE '' END
      || CASE WHEN next_food < food_floor THEN 'food would cross its floor; ' ELSE '' END
      || CASE WHEN next_soil < soil_floor THEN 'soil would cross its floor; ' ELSE '' END,'; ') AS stop_reason,
    json_object('day',day+1,'water',next_water,'food',next_food,'soil',next_soil,
      'beds',beds,'water_floor',water_floor,'food_floor',food_floor,'soil_floor',soil_floor) AS next_state
  FROM measured
)
SELECT source_id,before_state,next_state,safe,stop_reason,
  json_object('weather',weather,'rain',rain,'evaporation',evaporation,
    'spring',3,'drinking',2,'eaten',3,'irrigated',irrigated,'harvest',harvest,
    'compost',compost,'water_spilled',water_spilled,'food_spilled',food_spilled,
    'safe',json(CASE WHEN safe THEN 'true' ELSE 'false' END),
    'stop_reason',stop_reason,'proposed',json(next_state)) AS body
FROM judged;

CREATE VIEW proposal AS SELECT * FROM plans WHERE source_id=(SELECT id FROM head);

-- Independent historical validation also catches edits made with triggers removed.
CREATE VIEW audit AS
SELECT e.id,
  (e.id = coalesce(p.id,0)+1
   AND e.prev = coalesce(p.hash,printf('%064d',0))
   AND e.hash = lower(hex(sha3(json_array(e.id,e.stamp,e.kind,e.reason,json(e.body),json(e.state),e.prev),256)))) AS chain_ok,
  CASE e.kind
    WHEN 'genesis' THEN e.id=1 AND e.state=
      '{"day":0,"water":14,"food":10,"soil":6,"beds":2,"water_floor":4,"food_floor":4,"soil_floor":3}'
    WHEN 'tick' THEN coalesce(t.safe=1 AND e.state=t.next_state AND e.body=t.body,0)
    WHEN 'pause' THEN coalesce(t.safe=0 AND e.state=p.state AND e.body=t.body,0)
    WHEN 'policy' THEN coalesce(
      json_extract(e.body,'$.key') IN ('beds','water_floor','food_floor','soil_floor')
      AND json_type(e.body,'$.value') IS 'integer'
      AND e.state=json_set(p.state,'$.'||json_extract(e.body,'$.key'),json_extract(e.body,'$.value')),0)
    WHEN 'note' THEN coalesce(e.state=p.state AND e.body='{}',0)
    ELSE 0
  END AS transition_ok
FROM ledger e LEFT JOIN ledger p ON p.id=e.id-1 LEFT JOIN plans t ON t.source_id=p.id;

CREATE TRIGGER ledger_no_update BEFORE UPDATE ON ledger
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'receipts are append-only'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER ledger_no_delete BEFORE DELETE ON ledger
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'receipts are append-only'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER weather_no_insert BEFORE INSERT ON weather
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'weather is part of physics version 1'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER weather_no_update BEFORE UPDATE ON weather
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'weather is part of physics version 1'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER weather_no_delete BEFORE DELETE ON weather
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'weather is part of physics version 1'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER ledger_validate AFTER INSERT ON ledger
BEGIN
  SELECT CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM audit
    WHERE id=NEW.id AND chain_ok=1 AND transition_ok=1)
    THEN RAISE(ABORT,'receipt violates lineage or physics') END;
END;

#!/bin/sh
# Offline, bounded, transactional. Requires the sqlite3 CLI with JSON and SHA3.
set -eu
ROOT=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
STORE=${TENDORA_HOME:-"$ROOT/state"}
DB="$STORE/world.sqlite"

die() { printf '%s\n' "tendora: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
quote() { printf '%s' "$1" | sed "s/'/''/g"; }
header() { printf '%s\n' '.bail on' '.timeout 5000' 'PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON;'; }
input_table() { printf '%s\n' 'CREATE TEMP TABLE input(kind TEXT,reason TEXT,body TEXT,state TEXT);'; }

runtime() {
  command -v sqlite3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 'sqlite3 is required (no downloads are performed).'
  capabilities=$(sqlite3 :memory: "SELECT json_valid('{}')||':'||length(sha3('probe',256));" 2>/dev/null) \
    || die 'sqlite3 must provide JSON and SHA3 (the standard SQLite CLI does).'
  [ "$capabilities" = '1:32' ] || die 'SQLite JSON/SHA3 capability check failed.'
}

require_world() {
  [ -f "$DB" ] || die 'no world yet; run ./tendora init'
  version=$(sqlite3 -readonly "$DB" 'PRAGMA user_version;')
  [ "$version" = 1 ] || die "unsupported schema version $version; preserve this database and use its matching code."
}

count() {
  case "$1" in [1-9]|[12][0-9]|30) :;;
    *) die 'step budget must be an integer from 1 to 30 (without leading zeros)';;
  esac
}

setting() {
  case "$2" in 0|[1-9]|1[0-2]) :;;
    *) die 'a setting value must be an integer from 0 to 12 (without leading zeros)';;
  esac
  case "$1" in
    beds) low=0; high=3;;
    water_floor) low=2; high=12;;
    food_floor) low=3; high=12;;
    soil_floor) low=2; high=8;;
    *) die 'settings: beds, water_floor, food_floor, soil_floor';;
  esac
  [ "$2" -ge "$low" ] && [ "$2" -le "$high" ] || die "$1 must be between $low and $high"
}

reason_check() {
  [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ] || die 'give a reason for the receipt'
  [ "${#1}" -le 2000 ] || die 'reason must be at most 2000 characters'
}

policy_sql() {
  # Keys and integer values were checked before SQL generation; prose is quoted.
  printf "INSERT INTO input SELECT 'policy','%s',json_object('key','%s','value',%s),json_set(state,'$.%s',%s) FROM head;\n" \
    "$(quote "$3")" "$1" "$2" "$1" "$2"
  cat "$ROOT/sql/append.sql"
}

step_sql() {
  steps_left=$1
  printf '%s\n' 'CREATE TEMP TABLE halted(value INTEGER);' 'INSERT INTO halted VALUES(0);'
  while [ "$steps_left" -gt 0 ]; do
    printf "INSERT INTO input SELECT CASE WHEN safe THEN 'tick' ELSE 'pause' END,'%s',body,CASE WHEN safe THEN next_state ELSE before_state END FROM proposal WHERE (SELECT value FROM halted)=0;\n" "$(quote "$2")"
    cat "$ROOT/sql/append.sql"
    printf '%s\n' "UPDATE halted SET value=1 WHERE (SELECT kind FROM head)='pause';"
    steps_left=$((steps_left - 1))
  done
}

summary_sql() {
  cat <<'SQL'
CREATE TEMP TABLE report AS SELECT json_object(
  'mode',(SELECT mode FROM session),
  'requested_steps',(SELECT budget FROM session),
  'completed_steps',(SELECT count(*) FROM ledger WHERE id>(SELECT start_id FROM session) AND kind='tick'),
  'outcome',CASE WHEN (SELECT kind FROM head)='pause' THEN 'paused' ELSE 'complete' END,
  'start',json((SELECT state FROM ledger WHERE id=(SELECT start_id FROM session))),
  'end',json((SELECT state FROM head)),
  'receipt',json_object('id',(SELECT id FROM head),'hash',(SELECT hash FROM head)),
  'events',json((SELECT json_group_array(json_object('id',id,'kind',kind,'reason',reason,
    'body',json(body),'state',json(state))) FROM
    (SELECT * FROM ledger WHERE id>(SELECT start_id FROM session) ORDER BY id)))
) AS result;
SQL
}

run_steps() {
  # $1 = commit/rehearsal; $2 = budget; $3 = reason; $4/$5 = optional setting.
  {
    header
    printf '%s\n' 'BEGIN IMMEDIATE;'
    input_table
    printf "CREATE TEMP TABLE session AS SELECT id AS start_id,'%s' AS mode,%s AS budget FROM head;\n" "$1" "$2"
    if [ -n "$4" ]; then policy_sql "$4" "$5" "Rehearsal: $4=$5"; fi
    step_sql "$2" "$3"
    # Capture the exact transaction before releasing the writer lock. Report
    # only after commit, so another writer cannot change the reported outcome.
    summary_sql
    if [ "$1" = commit ]; then
      printf '%s\n' 'COMMIT;' 'SELECT result FROM report;'
    else
      printf '%s\n' 'SELECT result FROM report;' 'ROLLBACK;'
    fi
  } | sqlite3 "$DB"
}

verify() {
  quick=$(sqlite3 -readonly "$DB" 'PRAGMA integrity_check;')
  [ "$quick" = ok ] || die "database integrity failed: $quick"
  faults=$(sqlite3 -readonly "$DB" "SELECT count(*) FROM audit WHERE chain_ok IS NOT 1 OR transition_ok IS NOT 1;")
  [ "$faults" = 0 ] || die "$faults invalid receipts; preserve the database and inspect audit."
  structure=$(sqlite3 -readonly "$DB" "SELECT
    (SELECT count(*) FROM ledger WHERE kind='genesis' AND id=1)=1
    AND (SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_schema WHERE type='trigger' AND name IN
      ('ledger_no_update','ledger_no_delete','ledger_validate','weather_no_insert','weather_no_update','weather_no_delete'))=6
    AND (SELECT json_group_array(json_array(phase,name,rain,evaporation)) FROM (SELECT * FROM weather ORDER BY phase))=
    '[[1,\"Rain on the roof\",7,0],[2,\"Clearing\",3,1],[3,\"Sun through leaves\",0,1],[4,\"A still morning\",0,1],[5,\"Dry wind\",0,2],[6,\"A passing shower\",2,1],[7,\"Heat\",0,2],[8,\"More heat\",0,2],[9,\"The rain returns\",8,0],[10,\"A pale sky\",0,1],[11,\"Clear\",0,1],[12,\"Rain at dusk\",4,0]]';")
  [ "$structure" = 1 ] || die 'missing safeguards, genesis, or changed weather physics'
  sqlite3 -readonly "$DB" "SELECT 'Verified '||count(*)||' receipts: hashes, lineage, transitions, bounds, weather, and database integrity.' FROM ledger;"
}

snapshot() {
  sqlite3 -readonly "$DB" "BEGIN;
    SELECT json_object('format',1,'name','The Clearing','generated_at',strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ','now'),
      'head',json_object('id',(SELECT id FROM head),'hash',(SELECT hash FROM head),'state',json((SELECT state FROM head))),
      'next',json((SELECT body FROM proposal)),
      'weather',json((SELECT json_group_array(json_object('phase',phase,'name',name,'rain',rain,'evaporation',evaporation)) FROM (SELECT * FROM weather ORDER BY phase))),
      'events',json((SELECT json_group_array(json_object('id',id,'stamp',stamp,'kind',kind,'reason',reason,'state',json(state),'body',json(body),'hash',hash)) FROM (SELECT * FROM ledger ORDER BY id)))
    ); COMMIT;"
}

view() {
  # An external JS file permits opening index.html directly, without fetch/server.
  # Each forecast uses its own rolled-back transaction. Retry if a writer moved
  # the head between them, rather than mixing futures from different presents.
  mkdir -p "$ROOT/site" "$ROOT/.scratch"
  attempt=0
  while [ "$attempt" -lt 3 ]; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    original=$(sqlite3 -readonly "$DB" 'SELECT hash FROM head;')
    stage=$(mktemp "$ROOT/.scratch/snapshot.XXXXXX")
    {
      printf '%s' 'window.TENDORA_SNAPSHOT = {"world":'
      snapshot
      printf '%s' ',"futures":['
      run_steps rehearsal 12 'Compare one-bed care' beds 1
      printf '%s' ','
      run_steps rehearsal 12 'Compare two-bed care' beds 2
      printf '%s' ','
      run_steps rehearsal 12 'Compare three-bed care' beds 3
      printf '%s\n' ']};'
    } > "$stage"
    latest=$(sqlite3 -readonly "$DB" 'SELECT hash FROM head;')
    if [ "$original" = "$latest" ]; then
      mv "$stage" "$ROOT/site/snapshot.js"
      printf '%s\n' "Snapshot ready: $ROOT/index.html" "Authoritative head: $latest"
      return
    fi
    rm -f "$stage"
  done
  die 'world moved during export; retry ./tendora view'
}

help() {
  cat <<'HELP'
Tendora / The Clearing — a small world another hand can continue.

  ./tendora init                         Create genesis, once
  ./tendora status                       Present state and the next proposal
  ./tendora rehearse [1..30] [key value]   Run a future, then roll it back
  ./tendora tend [1..30] [--why TEXT]     Commit safe days; pause at a boundary
  ./tendora set KEY VALUE --why TEXT     Change an intention or boundary
  ./tendora note TEXT                    Leave an observation for a successor
  ./tendora history                      Read the receipts
  ./tendora verify                       Check lineage and replay the physics
  ./tendora view                         Refresh the offline visual workbench
  ./tendora checkpoint                   Save a consistent database + JSON copy
  ./tendora live [1..30] [1..60]          Bounded clock: days, seconds per day

Keys: beds (0..3), water_floor (2..12), food_floor (3..12), soil_floor (2..8).
Rehearsals print JSON; their receipt IDs/hashes are hypothetical, not saved.
TENDORA_HOME selects an isolated state directory (default: ./state).
No network, model calls, background service, or external actions are used.
HELP
}

command=${1:-help}
[ "$#" -eq 0 ] || shift
case "$command" in help|-h|--help) help; exit;; esac
runtime
case "$command" in
  init)
    [ "$#" -eq 0 ] || die 'usage: init'
    mkdir -p "$STORE"
    [ ! -e "$DB" ] || die 'world.sqlite already exists; init never overwrites it'
    {
      header
      printf '%s\n' 'BEGIN IMMEDIATE;'
      cat "$ROOT/sql/schema.sql" "$ROOT/sql/genesis.sql" "$ROOT/sql/append.sql"
      printf '%s\n' 'COMMIT;'
    } | sqlite3 "$DB"
    printf '%s\n' 'The Clearing begins at day 0. Three inhabitants; one shared garden.'
    ;;
  *)
    require_world
    case "$command" in
      status)
        [ "$#" -eq 0 ] || die 'usage: status'
        sqlite3 -readonly -line "$DB" "BEGIN;
          SELECT id AS receipt,stamp,kind,reason,state,hash FROM head;
          SELECT body AS next_proposal FROM proposal; COMMIT;"
        ;;
      rehearse)
        budget=${1:-12}; count "$budget"
        key=''; value=''
        case "$#" in
          0|1) :;;
          3) key=$2; value=$3; setting "$key" "$value";;
          *) die 'usage: rehearse [1..30] [key value]';;
        esac
        run_steps rehearsal "$budget" 'Rehearse a possible continuation' "$key" "$value"
        ;;
      tend)
        budget=1; reason='Continue the clearing within the chosen boundaries.'
        if [ "$#" -gt 0 ] && [ "$1" != --why ]; then budget=$1; shift; fi
        count "$budget"
        if [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; then
          [ "$#" -eq 2 ] && [ "$1" = --why ] || die 'usage: tend [1..30] [--why TEXT]'
          reason=$2
        fi
        reason_check "$reason"
        run_steps commit "$budget" "$reason" '' ''
        ;;
      set)
        [ "$#" -eq 4 ] && [ "$3" = --why ] || die 'usage: set KEY VALUE --why TEXT'
        setting "$1" "$2"; reason_check "$4"
        {
          header; printf '%s\n' 'BEGIN IMMEDIATE;'; input_table
          policy_sql "$1" "$2" "$4"
          printf '%s\n' "CREATE TEMP TABLE report AS SELECT 'Policy receipt '||id||': '||state AS result FROM head;" 'COMMIT;' 'SELECT result FROM report;'
        } | sqlite3 "$DB"
        ;;
      note)
        [ "$#" -eq 1 ] || die 'usage: note TEXT'
        reason_check "$1"
        {
          header; printf '%s\n' 'BEGIN IMMEDIATE;'; input_table
          printf "INSERT INTO input SELECT 'note','%s','{}',state FROM head;\n" "$(quote "$1")"
          cat "$ROOT/sql/append.sql"
          printf '%s\n' "CREATE TEMP TABLE report AS SELECT 'Observation saved as receipt '||id AS result FROM head;" 'COMMIT;' 'SELECT result FROM report;'
        } | sqlite3 "$DB"
        ;;
      history)
        [ "$#" -eq 0 ] || die 'usage: history'
        sqlite3 -readonly -header -column "$DB" "SELECT id,json_extract(state,'$.day') AS day,kind,
          json_extract(state,'$.water') AS water,json_extract(state,'$.food') AS food,
          json_extract(state,'$.soil') AS soil,reason FROM ledger ORDER BY id;"
        ;;
      verify) [ "$#" -eq 0 ] || die 'usage: verify'; verify;;
      view) [ "$#" -eq 0 ] || die 'usage: view'; view;;
      checkpoint)
        [ "$#" -eq 0 ] || die 'usage: checkpoint'
        mkdir -p "$STORE/checkpoints"
        destination=$(mktemp "$STORE/checkpoints/world.XXXXXX")
        copy_source="$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$STORE" && pwd)/world.sqlite"
        # Only the generated basename enters a SQLite dot command. Arbitrary
        # directory names (quotes, spaces, newlines) stay shell arguments.
        (cd -- "$STORE/checkpoints" && sqlite3 "$copy_source" ".timeout 5000" ".backup ${destination##*/}")
        # Inspect and export the COPY, so both files describe the same head.
        saved_db=$DB; DB=$destination
        verify
        snapshot > "$destination.json"
        DB=$saved_db
        printf '%s\n' "Checkpoint: $destination" "Portable observation: $destination.json"
        ;;
      live)
        budget=${1:-12}; interval=${2:-5}
        [ "$#" -le 2 ] || die 'usage: live [1..30 days] [1..60 seconds]'
        count "$budget"
        case "$interval" in [1-9]|[1-5][0-9]|60) :;;
          *) die 'interval must be 1..60 seconds (without leading zeros)';;
        esac
        trap 'printf "\nClock stopped. Committed receipts remain.\n"; exit 0' INT TERM
        while [ "$budget" -gt 0 ]; do
          clock_report=$(run_steps commit 1 'A bounded clock continued the clearing.' '' '')
          printf '%s\n' "$clock_report"
          clock_outcome=$(sqlite3 :memory: "SELECT json_extract('$(quote "$clock_report")','$.outcome');")
          [ "$clock_outcome" != paused ] || break
          # Respect a second caretaker's pause as well as this run's own pause.
          [ "$(sqlite3 -readonly "$DB" 'SELECT kind FROM head;')" != pause ] || break
          budget=$((budget - 1))
          [ "$budget" -eq 0 ] || sleep "$interval"
        done
        ;;
      *) die "unknown command: $command (try ./tendora help)";;
    esac
    ;;
esac

#!/bin/sh
# Behavioral checks, always in disposable worlds. No Python, Node or Git needed.
set -eu
ROOT=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
mkdir -p "$ROOT/.scratch"
TESTROOT=$(mktemp -d "$ROOT/.scratch/check.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -rf "$TESTROOT"' EXIT HUP INT TERM
export TENDORA_HOME="$TESTROOT/main"
DB="$TENDORA_HOME/world.sqlite"
passes=0
fail() { printf 'FAIL: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
pass() { passes=$((passes+1)); printf 'ok %s - %s\n' "$passes" "$1"; }
eq() { [ "$1" = "$2" ] || fail "$3: expected [$2], got [$1]"; }
cli() { "$ROOT/tendora" "$@"; }
query() { sqlite3 -readonly "$DB" "$1"; }
quote() { printf '%s' "$1" | sed "s/'/''/g"; }
json_field() { sqlite3 :memory: "SELECT json_extract('$(quote "$1")','$2');"; }
reject() {
  if "$@" > "$TESTROOT/rejection" 2>&1; then fail 'a forbidden operation succeeded'; fi
}
fresh() {
  export TENDORA_HOME="$TESTROOT/$1"
  DB="$TENDORA_HOME/world.sqlite"
  cli init > /dev/null
}

cli init > /dev/null
eq "$(query 'SELECT count(*) FROM ledger;')" 1 'genesis count'
eq "$(query "SELECT json_extract(state,'$.day') FROM head;")" 0 'genesis day'
cli verify > /dev/null
pass 'a fresh process can open and verify genesis'

before=$(cksum "$DB")
cli status > /dev/null; cli history > /dev/null; cli verify > /dev/null
eq "$(cksum "$DB")" "$before" 'read-only commands'
pass 'inspection leaves the database unchanged'

forecast=$(cli rehearse 12 beds 3)
eq "$(json_field "$forecast" '$.outcome')" paused 'rehearsal stops'
eq "$(json_field "$forecast" '$.completed_steps')" 3 'rehearsed days'
eq "$(json_field "$forecast" '$.end.soil')" 3 'protected soil'
eq "$(cksum "$DB")" "$before" 'rehearsal rollback'
pass 'an unsafe future is visible without changing one database byte'

cli set beds 3 --why 'Probe a larger harvest.' > /dev/null
actual=$(cli tend 12 --why 'Test the prediction against material.')
eq "$(json_field "$actual" '$.end')" "$(json_field "$forecast" '$.end')" 'prediction versus material'
eq "$(json_field "$actual" '$.completed_steps')" 3 'committed days'
eq "$(query 'SELECT kind FROM head;')" pause 'pause receipt'
eq "$(query "SELECT json_extract(body,'$.proposed.soil') FROM head;")" 2 'refused soil'
cli verify > /dev/null
pass 'committed continuation matches the rehearsal and preserves a refusal'

cli set beds 1 --why 'Give the exhausted soil a day of rest.' > /dev/null
cli tend 1 > /dev/null
eq "$(query "SELECT json_extract(state,'$.day') FROM head;")" 4 'resumed day'
eq "$(query "SELECT json_extract(state,'$.soil') FROM head;")" 4 'soil recovery'
eq "$(query "SELECT count(*) FROM ledger WHERE kind='pause';")" 1 'retained refusal'
cli verify > /dev/null
pass 'a consequential policy change resumes the world without erasing its pause'

before=$(cksum "$DB")
reject cli tend 31; reject cli tend 0; reject cli tend 08
reject cli rehearse 2 unknown 4
reject cli set soil_floor 9 --why 'Outside the physical range.'
reject cli set soil_floor 8 --why 'Above the current soil.'
reject cli set beds 2 --why '   '
reject cli init
eq "$(cksum "$DB")" "$before" 'rejected command atomicity'
pass 'budgets, settings, reasons, and impossible boundaries fail without mutation'

intention="A caretaker's probe; DROP TABLE ledger; --"
cli note "$intention" > /dev/null
eq "$(query 'SELECT reason FROM head;')" "$intention" 'literal prose'
cli verify > /dev/null
pass 'quoted intentions remain prose rather than SQL'

before=$(cksum "$DB")
reject sqlite3 "$DB" "UPDATE ledger SET reason='rewrite';"
reject sqlite3 "$DB" 'DELETE FROM ledger;'
reject sqlite3 "$DB" 'UPDATE weather SET rain=8;'
reject sqlite3 "$DB" 'INSERT INTO ledger SELECT id+100,stamp,kind,reason,body,state,prev,hash FROM head;'
eq "$(cksum "$DB")" "$before" 'immutable history'
pass 'direct rewrites and forged receipts are rejected by the database'

cli checkpoint > "$TESTROOT/checkpoint-report"
copy=$(find "$TENDORA_HOME/checkpoints" -type f ! -name '*.json' | head -n 1)
[ -n "$copy" ] || fail 'missing checkpoint'
eq "$(sqlite3 -readonly "$copy" 'SELECT hash FROM head;')" "$(query 'SELECT hash FROM head;')" 'checkpoint head'
eq "$(sqlite3 :memory: "SELECT json_extract(CAST(readfile('$(quote "$copy.json")') AS TEXT),'$.head.hash');")" "$(query 'SELECT hash FROM head;')" 'portable JSON head'
export TENDORA_HOME="$TESTROOT/restored"
mkdir -p "$TENDORA_HOME"
cp "$copy" "$TENDORA_HOME/world.sqlite"
DB="$TENDORA_HOME/world.sqlite"
cli verify > /dev/null
cli tend 1 > /dev/null
pass 'a checkpoint and its JSON agree, and the restored world continues'

fresh concurrent
cli tend 1 > "$TESTROOT/one" & one=$!
cli tend 1 > "$TESTROOT/two" & two=$!
wait "$one"; wait "$two"
eq "$(query "SELECT json_extract(state,'$.day') FROM head;")" 2 'serialized day'
eq "$(query 'SELECT count(*) FROM ledger;')" 3 'serialized receipts'
one_report=$(cat "$TESTROOT/one"); two_report=$(cat "$TESTROOT/two")
eq "$(json_field "$one_report" '$.completed_steps')" 1 'first budget'
eq "$(json_field "$two_report" '$.completed_steps')" 1 'second budget'
eq "$(json_field "$one_report" '$.events[#-1].state.day')" "$(json_field "$one_report" '$.end.day')" 'first exact report'
eq "$(json_field "$two_report" '$.events[#-1].state.day')" "$(json_field "$two_report" '$.end.day')" 'second exact report'
[ "$(json_field "$one_report" '$.end.day')" != "$(json_field "$two_report" '$.end.day')" ] || fail 'writers reported the same present'
cli verify > /dev/null
pass 'concurrent caretakers serialize without losing days or mixing receipts'

fresh tampered
sqlite3 "$DB" "PRAGMA ignore_check_constraints=ON; DROP TRIGGER ledger_no_update; UPDATE ledger SET reason=reason||' tampered' WHERE id=1;"
reject cli verify
pass 'verification detects damage even after an append-only trigger is removed'

fresh "space and 'quote"
cli checkpoint > /dev/null
cli verify > /dev/null
pass 'persistence works with spaces and apostrophes in the state path'

fresh clock
cli live 2 1 > /dev/null
eq "$(query "SELECT json_extract(state,'$.day') FROM head;")" 2 'bounded clock'
reject cli live 31 1; reject cli live 1 61
cli verify > /dev/null
pass 'the unattended clock has a finite budget and interval bounds'

fresh clock-pause
cli set beds 3 --why 'Probe the soil boundary with a bounded clock.' > /dev/null
cli live 6 1 > "$TESTROOT/clock-pause-report"
eq "$(query "SELECT json_extract(state,'$.day') FROM head;")" 3 'clock stops before unsafe day'
eq "$(query "SELECT count(*) FROM ledger WHERE kind='pause';")" 1 'single clock refusal'
eq "$(wc -l < "$TESTROOT/clock-pause-report" | tr -d ' ')" 4 'clock stops with unused budget'
cli verify > /dev/null
pass 'a clock stops at refusal even with time and budget remaining'

fresh seasons
cli tend 30 > /dev/null; cli tend 30 > /dev/null
eq "$(query "SELECT json_extract(state,'$.day') FROM head;")" 60 'continued seasons'
eq "$(query "SELECT json_extract(state,'$.water') FROM head;")" 12 'seasonal water'
eq "$(query "SELECT json_extract(state,'$.food') FROM head;")" 10 'seasonal food'
eq "$(query "SELECT json_extract(state,'$.soil') FROM head;")" 6 'seasonal soil'
cli verify > /dev/null
pass 'five complete weather cycles survive successive cognition-free runs'

printf '%s\n' "$passes behavioral checks passed; disposable worlds removed."
